title: The Chain Rule
summary: The chain rule differentiates a composition: $\frac{d}{dx}f(g(x))=f'(g(x))\cdot g'(x)$ — outer derivative times inner derivative. It is the key to handling anything 'inside' another function, from $\sin(x^2)$ to $(3x+1)^{10}$.

composition.in_class: Evaluate inner first, then outer; differentiate outer-times-inner.

chain rule.plain: Differentiate a composition by multiplying outer and inner derivatives.

outer function.in_class: You differentiate it first, keeping the inside intact.

Leibniz form.plain: The chain rule written with fractions.

general power rule.plain: Chain rule applied to a power.

nested composition.in_class: Apply the chain rule repeatedly, working outside in.

substitution u.plain: Naming the inside $u$ to organize the work.
substitution u.in_class: Let $u=g(x)$; then $y=f(u)$ and multiply the pieces.

concept_sections.heading: Recognizing a composition
concept_sections.explanation: A composition has an 'inside': $\sin(x^2)$ is $\sin$ of $x^2$; $(3x+1)^5$ is (something)$^5$. Spotting the inner function is the first step.
math_steps: Identify the last operation — that's the outer function.
What it acts on is the inner function.
Name the inner $u=g(x)$ if it helps.

concept_sections.heading: The rule
concept_sections.explanation: Differentiate the outer function (leaving the inside alone), then multiply by the derivative of the inside: $f'(g(x))\cdot g'(x)$.
math_steps: Do not forget the inner derivative — the most common mistake.

concept_sections.heading: The general power rule
concept_sections.explanation: For $[g(x)]^n$, bring the power down, lower it by one, and multiply by $g'(x)$: $n[g(x)]^{n-1}g'(x)$.
math_steps: Apply the power rule to the whole bracket.
Multiply by the derivative of the inside.

concept_sections.heading: Chain rule with trig and exponentials
concept_sections.explanation: $\frac{d}{dx}\sin(g)=\cos(g)\,g'$ and $\frac{d}{dx}e^{g}=e^{g}g'$. The inner derivative always tags along.
math_steps: Keep the inside unchanged in the outer part.

figure.caption: Chain rule with trig and exponentials

concept_sections.heading: Nested chains
concept_sections.explanation: For a composition of three or more, apply the rule repeatedly from the outside in — each layer contributes a factor of its own derivative.
math_steps: Multiply by the derivative of the next layer.

real_world_examples.title: Ripple radius and area
real_world_examples.scenario: A stone's ripple expands; its radius grows with time.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The area's rate of change combines area-vs-radius and radius-vs-time by the chain rule: $\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac{dA}{dr}\frac{dr}{dt}$.

real_world_examples.title: Temperature along a hike
real_world_examples.scenario: Temperature depends on altitude, altitude on time.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: How fast the temperature changes in time chains the two rates together.

real_world_examples.title: Compound effects
real_world_examples.scenario: Sales depend on price, price on a currency rate.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The overall sensitivity multiplies the intermediate rates — the chain rule in economics.
